nodes.title: Stable central distributions
nodes.statement: Define Z_st(G) as the complex submodule of Z(G) consisting of z with z(f)=0 for every f in U(G), where z(f) is distribution evaluation, not convolution as a test function.
hypotheses: E is a finite extension of Q_p; G/E is connected reductive. Fix Haar measures, a prime ell distinct from p, an isomorphism iota from Qbar_ell to C and the compatible square root of q for normalized Satake and induction.

H(G) consists of locally constant compactly supported complex test functions. D(G) is the complex span of finite-length Harish-Chandra characters; D_temp and D_ell use the harmonic-analysis supplier conventions. U(G) is the subspace of test functions with zero stable orbital integrals on the strongly regular semisimple locus.
proofSteps: Import the categorical Bernstein center from SR.3 and the unstable test-function space from ET.1. G1 must supply the essentially compact invariant-distribution realization, its pairing and the character quotient; the current upstream categorical-center plan alone does not provide this comparison.
Take the annihilator of U(G) inside Z(G); linearity of evaluation gives the submodule structure.
acceptance: The defining quantifier ranges over all unstable test functions; the ambient object is a submodule, with no claimed closure under multiplication.

nodes.statement: Z_vst(G) embeds in Z_st(G), and Z_st(G) is a module over Z_vst(G) under convolution. In particular the convolution of a very stable element with a stable element is stable.

proofSteps: For z very stable and f unstable, inversion gives another unstable function f^vee(g)=f(g^(-1)). Then z*f^vee is unstable; the G1 stable-delta_1 theorem and the usual distribution pairing give delta_1(z*f^vee)=z(f)=0.

Put z^vee(f)=z(f^vee). Inversion preserves U(G) and intertwines central convolution, so z^vee is very stable. For stable y and unstable f, (y*z)(f)=y(z^vee*f)=0. These identities follow by unfolding convolution on the unimodular group.

nodes.title: Hecke operators on virtual characters
nodes.statement: For dominant mu with 1 in B(G,mu), set F_mu=i_1^* T_(V_mu dual) i_(1!). Its bounded finite-length cohomology defines an Euler-class map on K_0 of finite-length smooth representations. After iota and complex linearization obtain T_mu:D(G)->D(G), with T_mu([A])=sum_j (-1)^j [H^j F_mu(A)]. The condition on mu is equivalently trivial action of Z(Ghat)^Gamma on V_mu.
